# S420 — Grok out of credits on stderr is classified, so the role falls back

When grok prints its credits or spending-limit error outside a stream event (on stderr or as a plain `Error:` line on stdout), the round's exit is out_of_credits with the same fixed reason as today, so the role falls back to the next matrix row and grok is marked out.

**Findings:** 2026-11-18 03:38 UTC: S388 (run ork-20261117-233556-f24d) implementer round 4 and gate round 5 ran grok-4.7 and each ended in under a second with exit "unclassified", no report, and the run stopped. A manual `grok -p "reply with ok"` (grok 1.0.77) printed `Error: Internal error: { "message": "API error (status 403 Forbidden): Your team <team> has either used all available credits or reached its monthly spending limit. ...", "http_status": 403 }` on its output and exited 0. The adapter looks for `used all available credits` only in stream `error` events (`internal/agent/grok/grok.go:291-309`) and sets out of credits only from that (`:380-381`), so the stderr form stays unclassified and the role neither falls back nor marks grok out. · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**2026-11-18** — Grok credits and usage-limit errors printed on stderr or as a plain stdout line now end out_of_credits with the same fixed reasons, so the role falls back and grok is marked out. A cleanly completed round and a permission-cancelled round are not scanned, so they keep their exits. Verified with new grok tests (stderr, plain stdout line, usage limit, clean round, permission cancel naming the text), mutation checks, go vet, gofmt and go test ./... (26 packages ok).

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

## Why

Two S388 rounds stopped the run on 2026-11-18 because grok's credit error went unclassified; the orchestrator had to probe grok by hand and mark it out. Classifying vendor failures is deterministic work, and owner rule (2026-11-17) says such steps are code.

## Failing tests

- `TestGrokCreditsOnStderrIsOutOfCredits` in `internal/agent/grok/grok_test.go`: a fake grok that prints the 403 `Error: Internal error: {...used all available credits...}` text on stderr, no stream events, exit 0; the round's exit is out_of_credits and the reason is the fixed text that does not name the team.
- `TestGrokCreditsOnStdoutPlainLineIsOutOfCredits`: the same text as a plain non-JSON stdout line; out_of_credits.
- `TestGrokBadModelAndAuthStayUnclassified` still passes.

## Implement

1. Write the failing tests and see them red for the stated reason.
2. After the process exits, if no stream event set credits, check stderr and any non-JSON stdout lines for `creditsText` and `usageLimitText` and set the same exits and fixed reasons as `fail` does.
3. Never copy the vendor message (it names the team) into the reason or a report.
4. CHANGELOG.md: one bullet at the end of `## Unreleased`, written by hand.

## Check

Acceptance criteria:
- A grok round whose credits or spending-limit error appears only on stderr or a plain stdout line ends out_of_credits, and the role falls back to the next row.
- The reason does not contain the team id.
- Other unclassified exits stay unclassified.

Commands:
- `go test ./internal/agent/grok -run 'TestGrokCreditsOnStderrIsOutOfCredits|TestGrokCreditsOnStdoutPlainLineIsOutOfCredits|TestGrokBadModelAndAuthStayUnclassified' -v`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test ./...`
- `gofmt -l .` must print nothing.
